Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

VCFArrow 0.10.0

  • New function vcf2fstructure(), an alias of vcf2structure() that writes the fastSTRUCTURE format by default (method = "F").
  • New function rename_vcf_samples() renames samples, from a named vector (c(old = "new")), a data frame or a file with columns id and new_id; by default each sample keeps its group, and update_groups = TRUE takes the groups from a pop column. The genotype files are rewritten, as sample names are stored with every genotype.
  • vcf_filter_adr() now changes only called heterozygotes: in "correct" mode an imbalanced heterozygote becomes the homozygote of its majority allele, and in "remove" mode it becomes missing. Previously any genotype with an ADR outside the threshold was affected, so "correct" filled in missing genotypes that had allele depths (AD), and "remove" set homozygotes to missing. It also reports the number of genotypes corrected or removed.
  • vcf_stats() (read_depth) and assess_vcf_coverage() use the read depth (DP) of called genotypes only. DP is sometimes written for missing genotypes which lowered the mean depth of samples with much missing data and added low depths to the coverage plot.
  • vcf_sub_SNVs_stratified() now returns exactly n_SNVs SNVs. Each CHROM contributes its proportional share rounded down, and the remaining SNVs come from the CHROMs with the largest remainders. Previously each share was only rounded down, so CHROMs with few variants contributed none: with DiscoSnp-RAD data, where nearly every variant has its own CHROM, no SNVs were returned. Subsamples drawn with a given seed differ from earlier versions.
  • vcf_filter_coverage() gains strict (default TRUE): called genotypes with DP below threshold, or without DP, are set to missing, as vcftools --minDP does, and their number is reported; no variants are removed, so follow with e.g. vcf_filter_invariant() and vcf_filter_missingness(). strict = FALSE gives the previous behavior: the genotypes are not changed, and only the variants with at least two called genotypes with DP >= threshold, polymorphic among them, are kept.
  • vcf_filter_oneSNV() gains by_quality (default FALSE): with TRUE it keeps the SNV with the highest QUAL of each block instead of the first. SNVs without QUAL rank last and ties go to the first SNV, so VCFs without QUAL (such as DiscoSnp-RAD output) give the default result, with a warning.
  • vcf2plink_bed() (and so vcf2admixture()) and vcf2plink_ped() with allele_code = "12" now write ALT as allele 1 and REF as allele 2, as PLINK does when it converts a VCF (plink --vcf): ALT is in column 5 of the .bim file and is coded 1 in the .ped file. PLINK’s A1 counts and frequencies therefore refer to ALT. Previously allele 1 was REF.
  • assess_vcf_coverage(): each violin now ends at the sample’s lowest and highest plotted depth (trim = TRUE) instead of extending beyond them.
  • vcf_suggest_chunk_size() now computes the memory of a genotype row from its columns, including the samples’ FORMAT text (new argument fmt_chars) and sample names (sample_chars), and shares the memory between workers (workers). It previously assumed 20 bytes per genotype, about a quarter of the real size, and so suggested chunks about four times too large. n_columns is deprecated and ignored.
  • vcf_memory_estimate(): the default chunk_size is now 50,000, as in read_vcf() (was 100,000).
  • vcf_filter_invariant() and vcf_filter_coverage() (with strict = FALSE) have a new argument strict_poly that sets what counts as polymorphic. With strict_poly = FALSE (the default) a variant is polymorphic if not all of its counted alleles are the same, e.g. both REF and ALT occur. With strict_poly = TRUE it is polymorphic if not all of its counted genotypes are the same, the previous behavior, which also removes variants where every sample is heterozygous. The functions that remove invariant variants after changing samples or genotypes (vcf_filter_missing(), vcf_extract_samples(), vcf_extract_groups(), vcf_filter_adr()) take the same argument, also with the default FALSE, so by default they now keep such all-heterozygous variants.
  • show() (printing a VCFArrow object) now reports the numbers of biallelic SNVs, multiallelic variants and indels, the samples per group, the number of chunk files, and the percentage of missing genotypes and the number of phased genotypes in the first chunk file that holds current variants. It previously always reported “Phased genotypes: FALSE”, and after filtering its FORMAT preview showed the first variants of the source VCF instead of the object’s own. The Arrow schema is no longer printed.
  • set_vcf_groups() is more robust:
    • samples not in the strata file get the group NA with a warning, and the other samples are still assigned; previously a single missing sample left every group NA;
    • an id assigned to more than one group, a missing id or pop column, or a missing file now stops with a clear error; previously a duplicated id or a misnamed column silently gave @groups the wrong length;
    • the file is read as tab-separated when its header line has a tab (so fields may contain spaces or be empty), otherwise as space-separated, and all columns are read as text, so numeric ids keep their leading zeros.
  • vcf_filter_missing() and vcf_filter_missingness() report the final percentage of missing genotypes over the retained variants and samples (with verbose = TRUE), as their documentation described; so do vcf_extract_samples() and vcf_extract_groups(). For the sample filters this reads the genotypes once more, which verbose = FALSE avoids.
  • read_vcf() reads genotypes correctly in cases it misread before:
    • GT is found by name in FORMAT, and all its alleles are read, including alleles of several digits (0/11, 10/2); previously the first three characters of the sample field were taken as the genotype, so haploid calls and lines without GT gave alleles taken from the next field (e.g. 1:5:... was read as 1/5) and 10/2 as 1/-1;
    • haploid genotypes are stored as homozygous (1 as 1/1);
    • genotypes with one missing allele (./1) or more than two alleles, and unreadable ones, are stored as missing, and a warning reports how many there were, together with lines without GT or with fewer sample columns than samples;
    • ADR is computed at biallelic sites only, so vcf_filter_adr() no longer changes genotypes at multiallelic sites, where the first two AD values need not be the genotype’s alleles;
    • DP, GQ and AD values in other notations (e.g. 1e2) are read correctly, and negative values are treated as missing;
    • chunk_size must be a positive whole number.
  • write_vcf():
    • the INFO fields AC, AN, AF and NS are recomputed from the samples and genotypes written, where present (new argument update_info = TRUE), so they stay correct after samples or genotypes were removed or changed;
    • variants without a valid position are not written (with a warning) instead of being written with the position -2147483648;
    • warns if the variants are not sorted by position (e.g. after vcf_bind(mode = "union"));
    • compresses by default when out_file ends in .gz;
    • adds a ##source=VCFArrow line to the header.
  • POS is stored as a double, so positions beyond 2,147,483,647 (chromosomes longer than 2.1 Gb) are kept instead of becoming NA. This adds 4 bytes per variant to the variant tables. vcf2genlight() stores such positions as NA (genlight positions are integers), with a warning.
  • vcf2eigenstrat() writes positions in the .snp file without scientific notation (e.g. 0.00004100, not 4.1e-05).
  • vcf_bind() (mode = "union" or outgroup = TRUE, absent_as = "missing"): genotypes absent from a source object are written by write_vcf() as ./. instead of ..
  • Exporters now write the formats their programs document:
    • vcf2bayescan(): each line starts with the locus number, as BayeScan requires (it was missing, shifting every column);
    • vcf2bayesass(): writes BA3’s native format, one line per individual and locus (indivID popID locID allele1 allele2, alleles 1 = REF, 2 = ALT, missing 0 0), and warns above BA3’s limits;
    • vcf2related(): each line starts with the sample name, and missing genotypes are 0 0 (were NA);
    • vcf2apparent(): each line starts with the sample name, and missing genotypes are -/- (were ?/?);
    • vcf2fineradstructure(): writes one line per RAD locus, defined as in vcf_filter_multiSNV() (new argument block_size), with each sample’s two haplotypes over the locus’s SNVs in RADpainter’s syntax (TGAT/CGAT, TGAT if both are the same, empty if missing), the genotypes taken as phased; it wrote one line per SNV with allele pairs such as A,C and NA,NA;
    • vcf2eigenstrat(): the .geno digits count copies of the reference allele (REF, column 5 of .snp), as EIGENSTRAT defines them; they counted ALT copies;
    • vcf2eigenstrat(): new argument chrom_code; by default non-numeric CHROM (e.g. contig names) is numbered 1, 2, 3, … in the .snp file, as EIGENSOFT needs integer chromosomes, with the mapping written to <out_file>.chrommap, and a warning gives the numchrom to set when there are more than 22 codes;
    • vcf2migrate() follows the Migrate-N manual’s data file format:
      • the first line gives the number of loci (blocks), not of SNVs, and for method "N" starts with the data type N (SNPs);
      • the loci are labelled (sK) for method "S" and (nK) for method "N" throughout (method "S" labelled its last block (nK), method "N" all blocks (sK)), and for method "N" the block lengths follow the order of the sequences (they were listed in sorted CHROM order);
      • individual names are written in a fixed field of 10 characters, with a warning giving the nmlength to set for longer names (they were followed by a tab, which Migrate-N would read as part of the name);
      • population names starting with a number are an error;
      • method "C" writes allele counts in Migrate-N’s HapMap format (data type H: position, REF and ALT with their counts, and the total); its previous format is not one Migrate-N documents;
      • method "C" leaves out SNPs without called alleles in some population (with a warning): Migrate-N crashes on them;
    • vcf2genepop(): each population starts with Pop alone on its line, as GENEPOP documents it (adegenet::read.genepop() failed on pop WA); the new argument pop_names = TRUE writes pop <group> as before;
    • vcf2smartsnp(): the genotype file has no header line, as smartsnp requires (smart_pca() failed on it); the samples and their groups, in column order, are written to <out_file without extension>_samples.smartsnp for smartsnp’s sample_group;
    • vcf2plink_ped(): new argument allele_code; "12" writes alleles as 1 (REF) and 2 (ALT), the only .ped coding ADMIXTURE reads;
    • vcf2treemix(): compresses the file with gzip, as TreeMix expects, when out_file ends in .gz (new argument gzip);
    • vcf2structure(): the documentation describes the file layout and notes that fastStructure adds .str to its --input name;
    • locus names (GENEPOP, BA3, EIGENSTRAT, Migrate-N, genlight) are CHROM_POS wherever the ID is missing, empty or .; previously only when every ID was missing, so a VCF with . IDs gave . for all loci;
    • vcf2genlight(): ploidy other than 2 gives a warning and is set to 2, as the genotypes are diploid.
      • vcf2snapp() declares the data as DATATYPE=INTEGERDATA SYMBOLS="012" instead of DATATYPE=DNA: BEAST 2 reads DNA data as nucleotides, whose alphabet has no 0, 1 or 2.

VCFArrow 0.9.1

  • vcf_theta() (and vcf_stats(theta = TRUE)): per-site nucleotide diversity now uses the unbiased estimator n/(n - 1) * 2p(1 - p) for n called alleles, as vcftools (--site-pi) and tidypopgen (loci_pi()) do. Values of pi are therefore higher than in 0.9.0 by the factor n/(n - 1), most for small groups; Watterson’s theta is unchanged.
  • vcf_stats() reports each sample’s inbreeding coefficient F, the method-of-moments estimate of vcftools and PLINK (--het), with the numbers of sites and of observed and expected homozygotes it is based on, and the mean F of each sample group (columns F, F_sites, F_hom_obs, F_hom_exp and F_group_mean). The new argument f_ref takes the allele frequencies from all samples ("all", the default) or from each sample’s group ("group").

VCFArrow 0.9.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-16

  • Initial CRAN submission.

Reading and storage

  • read_vcf() reads plain or gzip-compressed VCF files (including large DiscoSnp-RAD output) into a VCFArrow S4 object. Variant information is kept in memory; genotypes are written to disk as an ‘Apache Arrow’ dataset in chunks and read lazily, so datasets larger than memory can be processed.
  • set_vcf_groups() assigns samples to groups (populations); vcf_copy() makes an independent copy; vcf_gc() deletes the on-disk data of objects that are no longer referenced.
  • vcf_memory_estimate() estimates the memory an export needs, and vcf_suggest_chunk_size() suggests a chunk size for read_vcf() for the available memory.

Filtering, subsetting and merging

  • Variant filters: vcf_filter_quality(), vcf_filter_pass(), vcf_filter_biallelic(), vcf_filter_indels(), vcf_filter_coverage(), vcf_filter_maf(), vcf_filter_hets(), vcf_filter_missingness(), vcf_filter_invariant(), vcf_filter_oneSNV() and vcf_filter_multiSNV() (SNV blocks), and, for DiscoSnp-RAD data, vcf_filter_rank(), vcf_filter_rpt() and vcf_filter_paralogs().
  • Sample filters and subsets: vcf_filter_missing(), vcf_extract_samples(), vcf_extract_groups(), vcf_sub_SNVs() and vcf_sub_SNVs_stratified().
  • vcf_filter_adr() corrects or removes genotypes with an extreme allele depth ratio (ALT / (REF + ALT)): they are changed to homozygous or set to missing.
  • vcf_bind() merges objects with the same or different samples, matching variants by CHROM, POS, REF and ALT, in "intersect" or "union" mode, with an ingroup/outgroup mode (outgroup = TRUE) and optional recovery of previously filtered loci (recover_loci = TRUE). vcf_bind_sparse() is a deprecated alias of vcf_bind(..., recover_loci = TRUE).

Statistics and plots

  • vcf_stats() computes per-sample statistics (heterozygosity, missing data, depth) and, optionally, Watterson’s theta and nucleotide diversity per group (vcf_theta()), accumulated chunk by chunk with little memory.
  • assess_vcf_missing_data() writes a table and plots of missing data per sample, and assess_vcf_coverage() plots of read depth per sample (PDF, PNG and SVG).

Writing and conversion

  • write_vcf() writes plain or gzip-compressed VCF files.
  • Converters to the input formats of population-genetic and phylogenetic software: vcf2admixture(), vcf2apparent(), vcf2arlequin(), vcf2bayesass(), vcf2bayescan(), vcf2eigenstrat(), vcf2fasta(), vcf2fineradstructure(), vcf2genepop(), vcf2migrate(), vcf2nexus(), vcf2plink_bed(), vcf2plink_ped(), vcf2related(), vcf2smartsnp(), vcf2snapp(), vcf2snmf(), vcf2structure() and vcf2treemix(); vcf2gt_long() writes a long genotype table (CSV, feather or Parquet) and vcf2genlight() returns an ‘adegenet’ genlight object.

Performance

  • vcf_set_workers() runs the per-chunk work of reading, filtering, statistics, merging and exporting on background R processes. Results do not depend on the number of workers.
  • Performance-critical steps (VCF parsing, per-sample counts, theta and pi, writers of the exported formats) are implemented in C++.

Dependencies

  • ‘adegenet’ (for vcf2genlight()) and ‘svglite’ (for SVG plots) are suggested rather than imported; without ‘svglite’, SVG plots are written with R’s Cairo device.
